findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Outturn Report 25-26
findings.headline: Interest rate outlook highly uncertain due to Iran-Israel conflict; forecaster predicts upside risk to Bank Rate with potential hikes in coming months
findings.detail: The report notes the Iran-Israel conflict (started late February 2026) has driven commodity prices higher and created 'highly uncertain' economic outlook. Arlingclose's forecast is 'heavily weighted to the upside – i.e. there may be Bank Rate hikes', potentially as early as the next MPC meeting.
findings.matters: Rate rises would materially worsen debt service costs across the £99.72m borrowing portfolio; timing is acute given the July LOBO refinancing and forecast 2026-27 borrowing of £30.37m would be taken at potentially higher rates.
findings.figures: Bank Rate currently 3.75% (held since December 2025); CPI 3.3% (March 2026); upside risks flagged in March 2026 forecast
findings.quote: In the short term, the forecast is heavily weighted to the upside – i.e. there may be Bank Rate hikes.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Outturn Report 25-26
findings.headline: Capital Financing Requirement forecast to rise £21.21m year-on-year to £203.77m (2026-27), driven by capital programme commitments
findings.detail: The CFR—the cumulative capital expenditure financed by borrowing—is forecast to increase from £182.56m (31 March 2026) to £203.77m (31 March 2027). The council notes this assumes no new schemes are added; any additional capital requiring debt finance will increase CFR further.
findings.matters: Rising CFR indicates expanding capital commitments funded by debt; limits debt capacity and signals extended period of elevated borrowing requirements, increasing refinancing and interest rate risk.
findings.figures: CFR: £182.56m (31 March 2026) → £203.77m (31 March 2027) → £203.11m (31 March 2028); £21.21m year-on-year increase
findings.quote: The CFR is anticipated to increase in the next year assuming capital expenditure is incurred as currently anticipated.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Outturn Report 25-26
findings.headline: Liability benchmark forecasts £30.37 million additional borrowing requirement in 2026-27, up sharply from £55.45m at year-end
findings.detail: The council's liability benchmark—the estimated minimum borrowing needed to fund capital plans while maintaining liquidity—forecasts a need to borrow £30.37m in 2026-27. This is substantially higher than the £55.45m benchmark at 31 March 2026, indicating material new borrowing will be required.
findings.matters: Represents a material increase in external financing need for the coming year; combined with maturing debt (£7.79m PWLB + £0.40m Salix in 2026-27) and the July LOBO refinancing, creates substantial near-term borrowing demand.
findings.figures: Liability benchmark 2026-27: £121.90m forecast vs £55.45m actual at 31 March 2026; new borrowing need £30.37m
findings.quote: The liability benchmark indicates the Council may need to borrow £30.37 million during 2026-27, however this will be subject to the level of capital expenditure during the year and the level of reserves held and will be monitored on a regular basis.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Outturn Report 25-26
findings.headline: £19.25 million LOBO loans callable at 22 July 2026, requiring immediate refinancing decision
findings.detail: The council holds LOBO (Lender's Option Borrower's Option) loans totalling £19.25m that the lender can call on 22 July 2026. The council notes it has sufficient funds to repay but will need to refinance by taking out new debt. This represents a material near-term refinancing requirement just four months away.
findings.matters: A sudden £19.25m refinancing requirement tests market confidence and reveals current appetite to lend to this council at potentially higher rates in an uncertain interest environment.
findings.figures: £19.25 million LOBO loans, callable date 22 July 2026, full term maturity 22 January 2054
findings.quote: It is anticipated that this right may be exercised at the next call date, July 2026, and whilst the Council currently has sufficient funds to repay the loans, it will need to consider taking out new debt to replace them.

findings.headline: 2026-27 capital programme requires £9.456 million of unsupported borrowing and £3.849 million supported borrowing
findings.detail: Of the £52.687 million of BCBC resources funding the 2026-27 programme, £13.305 million is new borrowing (unsupported and supported combined). The council is also dependent on £18.186 million of capital receipts and £18.410 million of earmarked reserves, meaning one-off funding sources account for 70% of BCBC resources.
findings.matters: Reliance on borrowing and one-off capital receipts and reserves to fund current capital spending indicates limited recurring resources and potential future pressure on revenue budgets from borrowing costs
findings.figures: Unsupported borrowing £9.456 million; Supported borrowing £3.849 million; Capital receipts £18.186 million; Earmarked reserves £18.410 million; Total BCBC resources £52.687 million
findings.quote: BCBC Resources: Capital Receipts 18,186; Earmarked Reserves 18,410; Unsupported Borrowing 9,456; Supported Borrowing 3,849; Other Loans 2,370; Revenue Contribution 416; Total BCBC Resources 52,687
